What happens here

This is QSC's second facility, wholly dedicated to paint and body and operating as the Fast Painting workshop. All painting, body repair, color matching and chassis measurement happens here — usually starting with a photo assessment.

A tour of the facility follows the same journey the car takes: the reception and assessment area where damage is examined, documented and scoped; the body bay with chassis-measurement equipment and aluminium- and steel-correct repair tooling; the color lab where your car's paint is measured spectrally and test cards are sprayed; the controlled spray booths; and finally the finishing area where the result is flatted, polished and inspected under multiple light sources before you get the call.

The 'Fast Painting' name comes from how the facility is organized, not from hurried work: photo assessment cuts out exploratory visits, a pre-agreed scope eliminates surprises, and disciplined scheduling means your car does not sit in a queue but enters when its team and equipment are ready for it. Preparation and curing stages always take their full time — because shortcuts there surface, literally, within months.

FAQ

Frequently asked questions

Why does QSC run two separate workshops?

Because the two crafts conflict in one building: dust from mechanical work is the enemy of paint, and paint operations have no place beside engine repair. Separate facilities mean each team, space and set of equipment serves one discipline done properly.

Which workshop should I go to?

Engine, gearbox, electrical, AC, diagnostics, suspension or scheduled service → the maintenance workshop. Paint, dents, scratches, collision or body damage → the painting & bodywork workshop. Unsure? Call the main line and the team routes you.

Can one workshop move my car to the other if it needs both?

Yes — transfers between the facilities are handled by QSC with the same documented handover as any pickup, and you are kept informed at each step.
